newsitem.title: USA: Amoco to proceed with deepwater project.
newsitem.headline: Amoco to proceed with deepwater project.

text.p: Amoco Corp and Shell Deepwater Development Inc said in a release received here they plan to develop a significant deepwater Gulf of Mexico oil and natural gas discovery.
Production on the $500 million Marlin prospect project is expected to begin in mid-1995, the companies said.

The discovery was drilled in 1993 and is on Viosca Knoll Block 915 in 3,240 feet of water. Amoco is the operator and has a 75-percent working interest in the field which is located about 100 miles south of Mobile, Ala. Shell, part of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, owns the remaining stake.
Marlin ultimately is expected to produce 250 million cubic feet of gas and 40,000 barrels of oil daily.

"The deepwater Gulf of Mexico is a significant, strategic growth area for Amoco," said David Welch, Amoco vice president of the Gulf of Mexico business unit. He said Amoco "plans to aggressively pursue additional deepwater opportunities it has identified."
Several other strategic projects have been announced recently that support both Marlin and Amoco's other opportunities in the Gulf of Mexico, Amoco said.

Two new pipeline systems will transport Marlin production to onshore markets. The Main Pass Oil Gathering System, an Amoco-operated system installed in 1996, will transport oil production into the Empire, La. market.

Natural gas will flow through the recently announced joint venture Destin Pipeline, a joint venture of Amoco, Shell and Sonat Inc. The Destin Pipeline will come ashore at Pascagoula, Miss., where an Amoco/Shell gas processing facility will be built. The pipeline will extend northward to interconnect with five interstate pipelines in Mississippi.
